questions.question: Which inference platform billing model is most cost-effective for a workload running at less than 30% sustained GPU utilization?
questions.explanation: Below ~30% sustained utilization, per-token pricing wins because you only pay for tokens consumed and avoid idle GPU charges. Per-minute billing is cheaper once you are saturating the GPU above that threshold.

questions.question: Which inference platform is described as Python-native serverless with per-second billing and sub-second cold starts via GPU snapshots?
questions.explanation: Modal is the Python-native platform: you decorate a function with @modal.function(gpu='A100') and deploy with one command. It uses per-second billing and achieves sub-second cold starts for small models with pre-warming.

questions.question: What differentiates Fireworks AI from other per-token GPU platforms regarding fine-tuned LoRA model pricing?
options: Fireworks charges a 2x premium for LoRA-served requests
Fireworks charges LoRA-served requests at the same rate as the base model
Fireworks requires pre-purchasing LoRA serving capacity separately
Fireworks does not support LoRA fine-tunes on its serverless tier
questions.explanation: The lesson explicitly names Fireworks' policy of charging fine-tuned LoRA requests at the base model rate as a real differentiator versus providers that charge a premium for custom adapter inference.

questions.question: Which platform was valued at $5 billion after its January 2026 Series E and is described as enterprise-polish-optimized with SOC 2 and HIPAA certifications?
questions.explanation: Baseten closed a $300M Series E at $5B valuation in January 2026 from CapitalG, IVP, and NVIDIA. It is enterprise-polish-optimized with SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA-readiness, and Truss model packaging.

questions.question: The lesson identifies a rule of thumb for when per-minute billing beats per-token billing. What is that threshold?
questions.explanation: The lesson states: for workloads above ~30% sustained utilization of a dedicated GPU, per-minute (Baseten, Modal) starts to beat per-token. Below that, per-token wins by avoiding idle charges.

questions.question: Which inference platform is built on Ray and is described as best for distributed Python workloads where inference is one node in a larger compute graph?
questions.explanation: Anyscale is built on Ray and uses RayTurbo as its inference engine. It is the right pick when the inference step is embedded in a larger Ray-native distributed Python workflow rather than a standalone service.
